title: Model assurance scorecards: messaging & sales scripts
body:
TL;DR: Draft messaging framework and sample sales scripts for a new Model Assurance Scorecard we want to surface in the Model Catalog. The scorecard communicates model quality, runtime compatibility, and expected unit economics to engineering buyers. Goal: give SEs and AE motion-friendly language to close decisions faster and reduce the back-and-forth on model evaluation requests.

Context and problem statement:
- Buying teams are overwhelmed by open model variability: accuracy on narrow tasks, hallucination rates, latency/cost tradeoffs and unknown operational quirks.
- Existing ‘verified profiles’ in the catalog are too checklist-y for technical buyers — they want quickly consumable, comparable signals tied to runtime outcomes (latency, cost, stability).
- Sales and SEs spend cycles running bespoke evals for every customer. We need a repeatable articulation that reduces custom eval asks and accelerates trust.

Proposed artifact: Model Assurance Scorecard (MAS)
- One-card summary per catalog model combining: Quality signal, Safety/hallucination band, Runtime compatibility badges, Economics band, Prompts/drift-sensitivity note.
- Score elements (short labels we’ll surface in UI and in one-pagers):
  - Quality delta (Qd): concise numeric: model vs baseline on reference eval set (e.g., +3.2% vs base open model)
  - Hallucination band (H): qualitative: Low | Moderate | High (with short examples)
  - Runtime compatibility (R): badges: "cpu-friendly", "gpu-optimized", "kv-cache-ready", "quantization-safe" (indicates validated paths in Redwood runtime)
  - Cost band (C): expected per-token relative band (S/M/L) and a representative p99 latency at 512 tokens
